recipes.name: Egg and Sausage Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package refrigerated crescent roll dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cook sausage in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, until evenly browned, 7 to 9 minutes. Drain and crumble into small pieces.
Mix beaten eggs, mozzarella, Cheddar, and oregano together in a large bowl.
Line the bottom of the prepared baking dish with crescent roll dough, then sprinkle crumbled sausage over top. Pour egg mixture over sausage.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg and Sausage Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This egg and sausage casserole is ideal for a weekend breakfast, and it’s simple to make with eggs, sausage, crescent roll dough, and two types of cheese!

video.description: A simple, cheesy egg casserole with a crescent roll crust.

review.reviewBody: I made this for the first time for a work function and everyone loved it. I did make a few changes to the recipe after reading some of the other reviews. I preheated the oven at 350 and gave the cressiant roles about a 7 minute head start. I also increased the amount of eggs to a total of 10 and added 3/4 of a cup of milk. Also I used Italian Seasoning instead of Oregeno. I baked the casserole at 350 for 25 minutes and then lowered the temperature to 325 for the last 20 minutes and the eggs set perfectly. I will definitly make this again, but I might try sage sausage instead of the maple Jimmy Dean sausage that I used. Also I cut the cheese to a total of two cups instead of four and used a blend of cheeses.

Really Good!! I made a few changes recomended by others. I used 10 eggs, 2 cups cheese (1 cheddar, 1 mozzarella), 3/4 cup milk and 1/2 tsp. Italian seasoning. I also pre-cooked the crescent crust and added red peppers to the sausage while it browned. There were not leftovers to take home!!

I have made this many, many times now for all kinds of events. I get asked for the recipe all the time.

It does seem to need some extra time to cook (especially if it is refrigerated overnight before baking, like I do). One easy way I have found to determine if it is done is to bake it in a glass pan. When the cresent roll dough is no longer sticking all over the base of the pan and forms air pockets in between, it's done. 

ENJOY! You will love this recipe.

Great recipe with modifications. Followed the recommendations of the other reviewers and used 10 eggs and only 1 cup each of cheddar and mozzarella. Also added 3/4 cup of milk to the egg/cheese mixture. I pre -baked the crescent roll dough for 7 minutes before adding the filling and it turned out perfect. Made it a day ahead for Easter and refrigerated overnight. Easter morning I just reheated it in a 350 oven for 30 minutes and it was perfect. My guests loved it. I was especially glad that I didn’t add the full amount of cheese. It was just the right ratio of egg to cheese by halving the amount.

Excellent! The family loves it and the recipe is going in our "Keeper" file. I used 10 eggs, 3/4 cup milk, 2 cups shredded cheddar and 2 cups shredded pepper jack cheese. I had 8 oz Jimmy Dean regular sausage and 8 oz Jimmy Deam maple sausage, so I used that. I precooked the crescent roll dough in the 9x13 dish at 325° for 14 minutes. I layered cooked sausage on top of precooked crescent roll dough, then I layered sauteed veggies (diced onions, diced red bell pepper and sliced mushrooms. Poured egg and cheese mixture on top (I also added to egg mixture 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning), cooked in preheated oven at 325° for 40 minutes. A HUGE hit!!!

I've been making this for years. The very first time I made it, I did it exactly as written. It was too bland and had too much cheese. I've experimented and tweaked the recipe since then. As others have said, I pre- bake the crescent roll bottom at 350* for 7 minutes. It makes it so much easier to be able to get the Crescent Roll Dough Sheets to line the bottom of the pan! I use half the cheese amounts (1 cup each instead of 2), and I add some additional ingredients to the beaten eggs - salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, chopped onion, minced garlic, and sliced, fresh mushrooms. I bake it at 350*. It sets up better at the higher temperature.

Merry Christmas! I gave it 4 stars because of my adaptions!! And some good suggestions from others. Added the layer of croissant dough and baked 350 for 7 minutes., added a layer of sautéed chicken sausage,garlic, mushrooms, sweet onion, sweet peppers and spinach with Italian seasonings, S&P. Then only used 2 cups cheeses; mozz, cheddar, parm, whatever I had in the fridge; with 10 eggs and 1/2 cup whole milk. Baked 350 for 25 mins, 325 for 15 mins and was perfect! Everyone LOVES! ❤️

Super easy and yummy. After reading several reviews, ended up using 12 eggs, 3/4 cup milk and a little less cheese. Also added in a small package of diced ham and some Mrs Dash seasoning. Also baked crescent dough 8 minutes first then added egg mixture then baked for another 35 minutes at written temperature, came out great.

The first time I made this I followed the recipe to the letter, it was bland and no one went back for seconds. This time I used 10 eggs, 1 cup each of the cheeses, 3/4 cup milk, medium spicy sausage, the oregano, and I added a green pepper. I baked it for 25 minutes at 350, then 20 minutes at 325. This time it was a hit, everyone was fighting for seconds.

Followed others' modifications: precooked crescent dough for 7 minutes, increased eggs to 10, decreased cheese by half, added 1/3 cup milk and used a full lb sausage. First time, made a mistake and used a smaller dish with crescent dough up the sides (like a pie) and that burnt the crust. Will use the 9x12 pan and just have dough across the bottom next time.

I sautéed one medium onion with the sausage. I followed others and 1) used 10 eggs and 3/4 cup milk 2) baked the crescent rolls 7 minutes ahead and 3) baked the casserole at 350 for 25 minutes and then lowered the temperature to 325 for the last 20 minutes, 4) I cut the cheese to a little over 1 cup instead of four and used Mexican cheese blend. I made two casseroles: for the first I made as above. For the second, I boiled six potatoes ahead of time, let them cool, and then grated them into the bottom of the dish with a little salt and pepper. Both came out great and are easy ways to feed a crowd!
Loved this...used a few of the top-rated tweaks and family enjoyed it!! Shout out to ANGIEGAL for suggesting the clear glass pyrex to easily check the doneness of the bottom crescent dough👍

Made this for our camping weekend also, I received high praise from my 5-year-old grandson, many thumbs up, very easy I am sure you can add veggies or mushrooms in this, but if you have a picky eater, this is perfect.
I’ve been making this recipe for years. I also add a well drained can of Rotel. I use mild version. I rarely use crescent rolls unless I have some on hand. It’s delicious either way.
This is easy and great! Don't skip the oregano. It gives an extra amazing flavor!
Recipe is awesome! The only thing I did differently was add less cheese. I used half the amount of each cheese. It was cheesy enough for my family and me.
Make this for a church breakfast. It was a hit. I followed some of the other reviews and pre-baked the croissant dough, added Italian seasoning, diced onions and green peppers.
Easy to make, if not the quickest to cook. Simple, delicious flavors that will please picky eaters. Good for kids and families.
I have very picky grandkids, and husband I let my 2 grandkids help they were amazed how simple it was to make but needless to say they ate it all up thank you.
This was great. I rushed home Christmas Eve, the stores were closed, but I had everything I needed for this recipe on hand. It reheats very well.
